provenance: ANONYMOUS GET on https://oos.eu-west-2.outscale.com/<name-that-does-not-exist>. No credentials were sent, so the request carries no AWS Signature v4 and is attributed to no account: nothing was created, nothing was modified, nothing was billed, and the user's Outscale account was offered and deliberately not used. This is the same method that produced ScalewayMissingBucket (anonymous fr-par GET) and ExoscaleMissingBucket (anonymous ch-gva-2 GET), and it is the cheapest measurement that can settle a wire shape: the 404 body IS the subject. One request, read-only.
redaction: The request identifier of the recorded exchange is kept because it is the shape that matters here: x-amz-id-2 and x-amz-request-id carried the SAME value, which neither of the two existing dialects does. It identifies no account and names no resource. The bucket name was a timestamped nonce and is replaced below.
why_it_cannot_be_guessed: <Resource> is PRESENT and EMPTY — Scaleway fills it with /<bucket>, Exoscale omits it entirely.
<BucketName> is ABSENT — both other dialects carry it.
x-amz-id-2 equals x-amz-request-id — Scaleway and Exoscale derive them separately.
The message carries a final period, like Exoscale and unlike Scaleway.
server_header: nginx/1.20.0, so this is Outscale's own implementation rather than AWS S3
